The authors use the anelastic approximation to model the fully compressible fluid equations, which relaxes the assumptions of the Boussinesq approximation used in previous studies.

The authors find a sequence of bifurcations leading to the breaking of spatial symmetries as baroclinicity Z is increased, with transitions from simple axisymmetric flows to more complex non-axisymmetric and time-dependent states.
At low baroclinicity Z < 6x10^4, the kinetic energies grow quadratically with Z, indicating the dominance of toroidal motions.
The authors find regions of hysteretic bistability, where either of two distinct flow states can be realized depending on the initial conditions.
The dynamo solution obtained at Z = 17x10^4 and Pm = 16 has a large-scale dipolar magnetic field topology, with the magnetic energy density comparable to the poloidal kinetic energy density.
The azimuthally-averaged toroidal magnetic field shows a pair of hook-shaped flux tubes in the outer layer of the shell and a pair of flux tubes in the polar regions.
The authors argue that magnetic fields in stably stratified stellar interiors may not necessarily be of fossil origin, and that dynamo action may occur in the radiative zones of rotating stars.
